cards.name: ExtendScript DOM (official Premiere scripting API)
cards.summary: Premiere's documented ES3 JavaScript object model rooted at `app`: projects, bins, sequences, tracks, clips, effect parameters, keyframes, markers and export. Synchronous (blocks the UI while it runs). Frozen since Premiere 23.0 but still working in 26.x; it is the surface AdobeBridge (pr_build.jsx) drives.
use_for: Building a whole edit from a JSON timeline: import, place, trim, keyframe, export
Setting effect parameters and keyframes after QE or the UI has applied the effect
Reading back what Premiere actually did (clip times, transition positions) to self-verify a build
cards.how: Runs inside Premiere only. Entry points: app.project, app.project.activeSequence, app.project.rootItem, app.encoder. Deliver code with a BridgeTalk relay from After Effects (see the BridgeTalk card), a CEP panel's evalScript, or the VS Code ExtendScript Debugger. Wrap the job in try/catch and write 'OK' / 'ERR ...' plus warnings to a result file.
cards.script_api: app, app.project (Project), ProjectItem, Sequence, Track, TrackItem, Component, ComponentParam, MarkerCollection/Marker, app.encoder (Encoder), Time
cards.limits: Changelog for 23.0: no further changes or improvements planned. The scripting guide's index says ExtendScript integrations stay supported 'through September 2026' (that window has now passed); Adobe's September 2026 developer blog says 'ExtendScripts are not affected' by the CEP-to-UXP transition, so treat it as working but frozen and re-test after every Premiere update. The guide recommends running scripts from CEP panels; command-line execution needs extra configuration, varies by platform and is not recommended. Verified working on the installed Premiere 26.0.2.2. Cannot add effects or transitions (needs QE or UXP), cannot set clip speed, has no nest call, cannot create adjustment layers or apply .prfpset presets. ES3 engine: no JSON object in some contexts (harvest_pr.jsx carries its own serializer).

cards.name: Script delivery to Premiere: BridgeTalk relay from After Effects
cards.summary: Premiere has no simple, documented command-line flag for running a script (the scripting guide says command-line execution needs extra configuration, varies by platform and is not recommended; Adobe recommends CEP panels). AdobeBridge runs a JSX in After Effects with `AfterFX.exe -r <absolute path>`, and that JSX forwards the Premiere script over BridgeTalk. Premiere reports back through files.
use_for: Running any Premiere ExtendScript job from Python without a panel
Harvesting effect lists and parameter ranges (pve/harvest_pr.py)
cards.how: In AE: if (!BridgeTalk.isRunning('premierepro')) BridgeTalk.launch('premierepro'); var bt = new BridgeTalk(); bt.target = 'premierepro'; bt.body = 'eval(decodeURIComponent("<URL-encoded script>"))'; bt.send(); The Premiere script writes `<result>.start` when it picks the job up and `<result>` ('OK' or 'ERR ...' plus one warning per line) when done; Python polls both files. app.setSDKEventMessage(text, 'info'|'warning'|'error') also logs to Premiere's Events panel.
cards.script_api: BridgeTalk (target 'premierepro'): new BridgeTalk(), bt.target, bt.body, bt.send(), BridgeTalk.isRunning(), BridgeTalk.launch(); AfterFX.exe -r <abs path>; app.setSDKEventMessage(message, decorator)
cards.limits: BridgeTalk mangles backslashes in the body, so URL-encode it. `-r` with a RELATIVE path is silently ignored. AE cold-started hidden runs the job and quits, killing the relay: start AE normally. After AE's exportAsMotionGraphicsTemplate, AE ignores later -r scripts (restart AE). Never open or close projects from an AE -r script. Other routes: a CEP panel's CSInterface.evalScript (CEP is deprecated, see the CEP card); a UXP plugin cannot run ExtendScript.

cards.name: Project lifecycle: newProject, openDocument, save, saveAs, closeDocument
cards.summary: Create, open, save and close .prproj files from a script.
use_for: Starting each build in a fresh project
Opening a template project that already holds assets the API cannot create (adjustment layer, styled caption track)
Saving a versioned copy for delivery
cards.how: app.newProject(path) creates and opens a new project (AdobeBridge does this per build). app.openDocument(path, suppressConversionDialog, bypassLocateFileDialog, bypassWarningDialog, doNotAddToMRUList) opens one. app.project.save() saves in place; app.project.saveAs(path) saves a copy and makes it active.
cards.script_api: app.newProject(path); app.openDocument(path, suppressConversionDialog, bypassLocateFileDialog, bypassWarningDialog, doNotAddToMRUList); app.project.save(); app.project.saveAs(path); app.project.closeDocument(saveFirst, promptIfDirty); app.isDocumentOpen(); app.isDocument(path); app.projects
cards.limits: openDocument can raise conversion, locate-media or warning dialogs that block a headless run: pass the bypass flags and keep the dialog watchdog running (pve/pr_dialog_watchdog.py). saveAs switches the active project to the copy. Auto-save folders appear beside the project.

cards.name: Media import: project.importFiles and bins
cards.summary: Imports media files (video, audio, stills, image sequences, .srt) into a bin (.mogrt files go through importMGT instead).
use_for: Bringing footage, VO, music, SFX, stills and SRT files into the project before placing them
Organising bins per chapter or asset type
cards.how: app.project.importFiles([paths], true, app.project.rootItem, false). It returns only true/false, not the new items: build a lookup from rootItem.children[i].getMediaPath() (normalise slashes and case). Bins: rootItem.createBin(name), item.moveBin(bin), bin.renameBin(name).
cards.script_api: app.project.importFiles(filePaths, suppressUI, targetBin, importAsNumberedStills); ProjectItem.children, getMediaPath(), createBin(name), moveBin(newParent), findItemsMatchingMediaPath(path, ignoreSubClips)
cards.limits: getMediaPath works only for atomic media (not sequences or AE comps). Semi-transparent RGBA PNG overlays render weaker than expected in Premiere (an 85%-alpha black dim darkened only about 38%): bake dims into an opaque plate or use an Opacity value instead.

cards.name: Dynamic Link: project.importAEComps / importAllAEComps
cards.summary: Links After Effects compositions into Premiere as live project items (edit in AE, Premiere updates). This is how AdobeBridge brings AE titles and heavy VFX shots into the Premiere cut.
use_for: AE-built title cards, maps, counters and VFX shots placed in a Premiere edit
Keeping AE as the VFX app and Premiere as the final cut
cards.how: app.project.importAEComps(aepPath, ['COMP_A', 'COMP_B'], app.project.rootItem). The new items' names start with the comp name: find them by name prefix, set in/out on the item, then overwriteClip onto a track.
cards.script_api: app.project.importAEComps(path, compNames, targetBin); app.project.importAllAEComps(path, targetBin); UXP: Project.importAEComps(aepPath, compNames, targetBin), Project.importAllAEComps(aepPath, targetBin)
cards.limits: Premiere cannot render Dynamic-Linked comps from an .aep that is open in the AE window: link to a COPY (AdobeBridge uses <name>_pr_titles.aep). Dynamic Link renders slowly; once a VFX comp is final, render it with aerender to ProRes and import the file. UXP importAEComps default-bin handling was fixed in 26.5.

cards.name: Sequence creation and settings
cards.summary: Creates sequences and sets frame size and frame rate.
use_for: 9:16 reels (1080x1920), 1:1 news cards, 16:9 documentaries and trailers from one script
Matching sequence fps to the delivery spec (25 for Indian broadcast-style, 30 for social)
cards.how: AdobeBridge pattern: seq = app.project.createNewSequenceFromClips(name, [firstItem], rootItem); st = seq.getSettings(); st.videoFrameWidth = W; st.videoFrameHeight = H; st.videoFrameRate = Time with seconds = 1/fps; seq.setSettings(st); remove every clip (while (track.clips.numItems) track.clips[0].remove(false, false)); app.project.openSequence(seq.sequenceID). Or app.project.newSequence(name, sqpresetPath) from a saved .sqpreset.
cards.script_api: app.project.createNewSequenceFromClips(name, projectItems[], bin); app.project.newSequence(name, pathToSequencePreset); app.project.createNewSequence(name, sequenceID); Sequence.getSettings() / setSettings(settings); app.project.openSequence(sequenceID); app.project.activeSequence; app.project.sequences
cards.limits: createNewSequence(name, id) may open the New Sequence dialog on some versions (unverified here); AdobeBridge avoids it. New sequences have 3 video + 3 audio tracks: add more with QE addTracks. QE always works on the ACTIVE sequence, so openSequence before any QE call.

cards.name: Placing clips: overwriteClip / insertClip with source in/out
cards.summary: Puts a project item on a track at a time, using the source range set on the project item.
use_for: Laying B-roll, interview bites, stills, music and SFX at exact times
Ripple-inserting a new shot (insertClip) versus overwriting a gap (overwriteClip)
cards.how: item.setInPoint(srcIn, 4); item.setOutPoint(srcIn + dur, 4) (mediaType 4 = video and audio); track.overwriteClip(item, startSeconds); then find the new TrackItem on that track by start time (within half a frame) and set trackItem.end to a Time at start + dur (needed for stills).
cards.script_api: ProjectItem.setInPoint(seconds, mediaType); ProjectItem.setOutPoint(seconds, mediaType); ProjectItem.clearInPoint()/clearOutPoint(); Track.overwriteClip(projectItem, timeSeconds); Track.insertClip(projectItem, time); Sequence.overwriteClip(projectItem, time, vTrackIndex, aTrackIndex); Sequence.insertClip(projectItem, time, vTrackIndex, aTrackIndex)
cards.limits: The calls return no TrackItem: look it up by start time. Snap every time to the sequence frame grid first (off-grid times broke the lookup). Source in/out persist on the project item: set them again before each placement. Placing A/V media may also lay its audio on an audio track (not verified here: check and remove if unwanted; TrackItem.getLinkedItems() appears in pymiere's reflection-generated API but is not on the docs page and is unverified here). The docs disagree on the time argument: Track.overwriteClip/insertClip say a ticks string, Sequence.overwriteClip says seconds, Sequence.insertClip says a Time object. The guide's own nestSelection example and AdobeBridge pass a seconds number to Track.overwriteClip, which works on 26.0.2.

cards.name: TrackItem timing and state: start, end, inPoint, outPoint, move, remove, disabled
cards.summary: Reads and edits a placed clip's timeline position, trim, enabled state and name.
use_for: Trimming a clip to a beat (end)
Shifting a clip later on its track (move)
Ripple-deleting a shot (remove with ripple)
Muting a layer for an alternate version (disabled)
cards.how: trackItem.end = Time (trim tail); trackItem.move(Time offset) shifts it (15.4+); trackItem.remove(true, true) ripple-deletes; trackItem.disabled = true; trackItem.name = 'label'.
cards.script_api: TrackItem.start, end, inPoint, outPoint (Time, read/write); TrackItem.duration (read); move(newInPointTime); remove(inRipple, inAlignToVideo); disabled; name; projectItem; mediaType; getMatchName(); isAdjustmentLayer(); getSpeed(); isSpeedReversed()
cards.limits: No razor, slip, slide or roll in the official DOM (QE has unsupported ones). How writing `start` behaves (move vs trim) was not verified here; AdobeBridge only writes `end`. getSpeed/isSpeedReversed/isAdjustmentLayer are read-only. See also: 'Trims: ripple, roll, slip and slide'; 'J-cut and L-cut (split edits)'; 'Closing gaps (Ripple Delete, Close Gap)'; 'Lift and Extract (remove a range)'.

cards.name: Effect parameters: Component and ComponentParam.setValue
cards.summary: Every clip's effects (Motion, Opacity, Volume, then applied effects in order) are Components; their controls are ComponentParams you read and set by display name.
use_for: Setting effect values from a PVE spec (pr_props)
Dumping a clip's full effect stack for QA (pr_build `dump`)
cards.how: Loop trackItem.components[k].displayName to find the effect (search from the END for one just added), then component.properties[k].displayName for the control; param.setValue(value, true). Repeated names (Lumetri has several 'Contrast', 'Intensity') are addressed in the PVE spec as 'Name#2' for the 2nd occurrence.
cards.script_api: TrackItem.components (ComponentCollection); Component.displayName, Component.matchName, Component.properties; ComponentParam.displayName, getValue(), setValue(value, updateUI)
cards.limits: Display names are localised (this install is English). Out-of-range values are clamped silently (the harvest probed every range by setting +/-1e9). Points are [x, y] frame fractions. Popup values are raw numbers, 0-based as harvested: take the range from the effect's card. Header/group rows have empty or group names and no value. Some params are opaque strings or JSON (Lumetri LookAsset, .mogrt text) and are not settable from the PVE spec. ExtendScript cannot remove a component (UXP can).

cards.name: Keyframes: setTimeVarying, addKey, setValueAtKey, setInterpolationTypeAtKey
cards.summary: Animates any keyframable ComponentParam (Scale push-ins, Position drifts, blur reveals, volume fades).
use_for: Ken Burns push-in or pull-out on stills (Motion > Scale)
Pan drifts (Motion > Position)
Blur-in or glow pulses on effects
Audio fades and dips (Volume > Level)
cards.how: param.setTimeVarying(true); for each key: param.addKey(t); param.setValueAtKey(t, value, true). t is in the clip's SOURCE time: add trackItem.inPoint.seconds to a time measured from the clip start (pr_build: k0 = ti.inPoint.seconds). Optional: param.setInterpolationTypeAtKey(t, 5, true) for Bezier. Interpolation constants: 0 linear, 4 hold, 5 bezier, 6 time, 7 time-transition start, 8 time-transition end (1-3 are obsolete eases).
cards.script_api: ComponentParam.setTimeVarying(bool); addKey(time); setValueAtKey(time, value, updateUI); setInterpolationTypeAtKey(time, interpolationType, updateUI); getKeys(); getValueAtKey(time); getValueAtTime(time); removeKey(time); removeKeyRange(start, end); findNearestKey(time, thresholdTicks); findNextKey(time); findPreviousKey(time); areKeyframesSupported(); isTimeVarying()
cards.limits: Docs type the time as a Time object; plain seconds numbers work on 26.0.2 (pr_build passes numbers). No control over ease speed/influence: Bezier is automatic. setTimeVarying(false) discards keys. setInterpolationTypeAtKey has not yet been exercised in AdobeBridge.

cards.name: Colour parameters: setColorValue / getColorValue
cards.summary: Sets colour controls (Tint colours, Fill, Stroke, Glow colour, .mogrt colours).
use_for: Brand saffron/green tints on lower thirds and cards
Recolouring .mogrt shapes and text
cards.how: '#RRGGBB' -> param.setColorValue(255, r, g, b, true). To detect a colour param, getValue() returns a packed number above 2^32 (that is how the harvest and pr_build tell colour params apart).
cards.script_api: ComponentParam.setColorValue(alpha, red, green, blue, updateUI); ComponentParam.getColorValue()
cards.limits: Keyframed colour values (setValueAtKey with a colour) are unverified. Components 0-255 integers.

cards.name: Intrinsic Motion and Opacity components
cards.summary: Every video clip carries 'Motion' (Position, Scale, Scale Width, Uniform Scale, Rotation, Anchor Point, Anti-flicker Filter, Crop Left/Top/Right/Bottom) and 'Opacity' (Opacity, Blend Mode), all scriptable.
use_for: Cover-fit scaling and push-ins on stills and footage
Picture-in-picture and split layouts (Position + Scale + Crop)
Fades via Opacity keys
Blend overlays (film grain, light leaks) via Blend Mode
cards.how: Motion > Scale (percent), Motion > Position [x, y] as frame fractions (0.5, 0.5 = centre), Motion > Rotation (degrees), Opacity > Opacity (0-100). AdobeBridge clip keys: zoom_from/zoom (Scale ramp), pan [[x,y],[x,y]] (Position), opacity_pct (value or keys).
cards.script_api: component 'Motion' params: Position, Scale, Scale Width, Uniform Scale, Rotation, Anchor Point, Anti-flicker Filter, Crop Left, Crop Top, Crop Right, Crop Bottom; component 'Opacity' params: Opacity, Blend Mode
cards.limits: Blend Mode is a raw number (dumps showed 0 and 18); the index-to-mode mapping was not harvested, so verify a mode before relying on it. Opacity masks (pen/ellipse) are not scriptable. Time Remapping did not appear in the component dumps (those were stills).
sources: live component dump from a production Premiere project (not published)

cards.name: Audio clip Volume and fades
cards.summary: Audio clips carry an intrinsic 'Volume' component whose 'Level' param sets gain and takes keyframes; fades and ducking dips are keyframes on it.
use_for: Music bed at -18 dB under VO
Fade in/out on music and SFX
Manual ducking dips under VO lines
cards.how: Level is LINEAR: value = 10^((dB - 15) / 20), so 0 dB = 0.1778. Fade = keys at 10^(-90/20) = 0.0000316 (that is -75 dB on this scale, 20 log10(v) + 15, not -90: inaudible either way) and the target level (pr_build fade_in/fade_out). Measured 2026-10-14 (live wave 3): 0.0562 = -10.0 dB, 0.1778 = 0 dB, 0.3162 = +5.0 dB, 1 = +15.0 dB. Find with components 'Volume' > 'Level'.
cards.script_api: audio TrackItem.components 'Volume' > 'Level' (setValue / addKey / setValueAtKey); audio effects via QE addAudioEffect
cards.limits: Mono clips get a further -3 dB pan-law drop. Channel Volume's rows are 'Left' and 'Right' on the same scale (0.1778 = 0 dB; stereo dump, live wave 3); the Panner's param names were not harvested. Track-level volume automation (Audio Track Mixer), Essential Sound tags and Auto-Ducking are not exposed by ExtendScript or the UXP reference; QE has nothing documented for them.

cards.name: Markers: sequence and clip markers
cards.summary: Creates, colours, types and reads markers on sequences and project items.
use_for: Beat or cut markers from a music analysis
YouTube chapter markers on long-form explainers
Review notes for a human editor
cards.how: var m = seq.markers.createMarker(seconds); m.name = 'Ch 2'; m.comments = '...'; m.end = seconds + dur (a seconds NUMBER: the docs say not to assign a Time object to end); m.setTypeAsChapter(); m.setColorByIndex(colorIndex) (documented as setColorByIndex(colorIndex, markerIndex), but Adobe's PProPanel sample passes only the colour index). Colours: 0 green, 1 red, 2 purple, 3 orange, 4 yellow, 5 white, 6 blue, 7 cyan. Read: getFirstMarker()/getNextMarker(m), numMarkers; clip markers via projectItem.getMarkers().
cards.script_api: Sequence.markers (MarkerCollection): createMarker(time), deleteMarker(marker), getFirstMarker(), getNextMarker(m), getPrevMarker(m), getLastMarker(), numMarkers; Marker.name, comments, start (Time), end (Time, write seconds), type (read-only string: Comment, Chapter, Segmentation, WebLink), guid, setTypeAsChapter(), setTypeAsComment(), setTypeAsSegmentation(), setTypeAsWebLink(url, frameTarget), getWebLinkURL(), getWebLinkFrameTarget(), getColorByIndex(), setColorByIndex(colorIndex, markerIndex); ProjectItem.getMarkers()
cards.limits: Whether chapter markers reach an exported MP4 depends on the export preset (unverified). UXP equivalent needs a transaction: Markers.getMarkers(seq).createAddMarkerAction(name, type, start, duration, comments).

cards.name: Render inside Premiere: Sequence.exportAsMediaDirect
cards.summary: Renders a sequence to a file with an .epr export preset, synchronously, without Media Encoder's queue.
use_for: Final MP4 of a reel or documentary at the end of a build
QC renders for frame checks
cards.how: seq.exportAsMediaDirect(new File(outMp4).fsName, new File(eprPath).fsName, app.encoder.ENCODE_ENTIRE). H.264 preset used here: C:/Program Files/Adobe/Adobe Media Encoder 2026/MediaIO/systempresets/4E49434B_48323634/00 - Match Source - High bitrate.epr. Then check that the output file exists.
cards.script_api: Sequence.exportAsMediaDirect(outputPath, presetPath, workAreaType) with workAreaType 0 = entire (app.encoder.ENCODE_ENTIRE), 1 = in to out, 2 = work area; Sequence.getExportFileExtension(presetPath)
cards.limits: Blocks Premiere until finished. workAreaType 2 needs the work area bar, which is off by default (check seq.isWorkAreaEnabled()). Needs NATIVE backslash paths (use File.fsName): forward slashes fail with 'Unknown Error'. The return value is not a reliable success signal: test the file. Dynamic-Linked comps from an .aep open in AE will not render (link a copy).

cards.name: Media Encoder queue: app.encoder
cards.summary: Queues sequences, project items or files to Adobe Media Encoder and starts the batch, so Premiere stays free while renders run.
use_for: Rendering several deliverables (9:16, 1:1, 16:9) from one build
Batch proxies or transcodes
cards.how: app.encoder.launchEncoder(); var id = app.encoder.encodeSequence(seq, outPath, eprPath, 0, true); app.encoder.startBatch(); then poll for the output files. Media Encoder 2026 is installed here.
cards.script_api: app.encoder.launchEncoder(); encodeSequence(sequence, outputPath, presetPath, workArea, removeUponCompletion); encodeProjectItem(projectItem, outputPath, presetPath, workArea, removeUponCompletion); encodeFile(filePath, outputPath, presetPath, workArea, removeUponCompletion, inPoint, outPoint); startBatch(); setSidecarXMPEnabled(enabled); setEmbeddedXMPEnabled(enabled)
cards.limits: Not yet used by AdobeBridge. encode* calls return a job ID string, or 0 on failure. Job events are used in Adobe's PProPanel sample: app.encoder.bind('onEncoderJobComplete' | 'onEncoderJobError' | 'onEncoderJobProgress' | 'onEncoderJobQueued' | 'onEncoderJobCanceled', fn), with onEncoderJobComplete(jobID, outputFilePath). They only reach a persistent script context such as a CEP panel, not a one-shot BridgeTalk job, so poll files instead (untested here). UXP equivalent: EncoderManager.getManager().exportSequence(...) / encodeFile(...). See also: 'Export encoding choices: VBR 2-pass vs CBR, maximum depth and quality, field order'; 'Colour tags on export: Rec.709 colr/nclc and the QuickTime gamma shift' and the 'Delivery spec: ...' cards (YouTube upload, vertical Reels/Shorts/TikTok, broadcast masters, mezzanine and archive masters, alpha overlays).

cards.name: Motion Graphics Templates: importMGT and getMGTComponent
cards.summary: Places a .mogrt on a track and edits its exposed parameters (text, font, size, colours, sliders, checkboxes, Duration).
use_for: Lower thirds, name straps, callouts, counters and shape animations in news and explainer edits
House templates exported from AE (make_house_mogrts.py)
cards.how: var ti = seq.importMGT(path, String(Math.round(startSec * 254016000000)), videoTrackIndex0, 0); var mc = ti.getMGTComponent(); text params are those whose getValue() is JSON containing 'textEditValue': o = JSON.parse(v); o.textEditValue = text; o.fontTextRunLength = [text.length]; optional o.fontEditValue = [postscriptName]; o.fontSizeEditValue = [size]; param.setValue(JSON.stringify(o), true). Set a 'Duration' param if exposed, then ti.end = Time. Colours with setColorValue. From CC Libraries: seq.importMGTFromLibrary(libraryName, mgtName, time, vOff, aOff).
cards.script_api: Sequence.importMGT(path, timeInTicksString, vidTrackOffset, audTrackOffset) -> TrackItem; TrackItem.getMGTComponent() -> Component; Sequence.importMGTFromLibrary(libraryName, mgtName, time, vidTrackOffset, audTrackOffset); UXP: SequenceEditor.insertMogrtFromPath(path, TickTime, vIdx, aIdx), insertMogrtFromLibrary(...)
cards.limits: The docs describe importMGT/getMGTComponent only for After Effects-authored .mogrts; templates made in Premiere's Essential Graphics are community-reported to return null from getMGTComponent (unverified here), so author house templates in AE. Premiere clamps .mogrt sliders to AE's 0-100 slider range (expose big numbers as hidden text). Text boxes with a locked font size need 'Scale'. Two .mogrts overlapping on one track overwrite each other: put them on separate tracks. Param names repeat ('Text' group, text, colour): match colours only on params holding a packed colour.

cards.name: Captions from SRT: Sequence.createCaptionTrack
cards.summary: Creates a caption track on a sequence from an imported caption file (.srt etc.).
use_for: Subtitle tracks for reels and YouTube explainers from a Whisper-generated SRT
Sidecar caption deliverables
cards.how: Write an .srt, app.project.importFiles([srt]), find its project item, then seq.createCaptionTrack(srtItem, 0, Sequence.CAPTION_FORMAT_SUBTITLE). Formats: CAPTION_FORMAT_SUBTITLE, _608, _708, _TELETEXT, _OPEN_EBU, _OP42, _OP47.
cards.script_api: Sequence.createCaptionTrack(projectItem, startAtTimeSeconds, [captionFormat])
cards.limits: Caption STYLING (font, size, position, background box) is not exposed in ExtendScript or the UXP reference: apply a saved caption style by hand, or build styled burned-in text with AE comps or .mogrts (what AdobeBridge does, including Hindi). Automatic speech-to-text exists only in UXP (Transcript.transcribeClipProjectItem, listed for 26.5, not on the installed 26.0.2): use local Whisper for SRTs. Devanagari shaping on caption tracks is unverified. Not yet exercised in AdobeBridge.

cards.name: Nested sequences (no direct Nest call)
cards.summary: There is no 'Nest' method in ExtendScript, QE (known) or UXP. Nesting is done by placing one sequence's project item inside another, or by createSubsequence plus replacement.
use_for: Applying one look or one Transform move to a group of shots
Pre-building a repeated intro or segment once and reusing it
Speeding or reversing a whole segment later by hand
cards.how: Build-time (preferred): build the inner sequence first, then place it with outerTrack.overwriteClip(innerSeq.projectItem, startSeconds). After the fact (the scripting guide's own nestSelection() example): set seq in/out to the selection's start/end seconds, var sub = seq.createSubsequence(true), then seq.videoTracks[trackIdx].overwriteClip(sub.projectItem, start.seconds) over the originals on that track, then restore the old in/out. Clips on OTHER tracks inside the range are not replaced: remove them yourself.
cards.script_api: Sequence.projectItem; Track.overwriteClip(projectItem, time); Sequence.createSubsequence(ignoreTrackTargeting); Sequence.setInPoint(time)/setOutPoint(time); UXP: Sequence.createSubsequence(ignoreTrackTargeting)
cards.limits: createSubsequence COPIES (the docs: 'This is not the same as nesting'); it does not replace the originals. Without ignoreTrackTargeting = true (default false), only targeted tracks are copied. Placing a sequence's projectItem via overwriteClip is documented in the guide's example but not yet run in AdobeBridge.

cards.name: Auto Reframe sequence: Sequence.autoReframeSequence
cards.summary: Generates a new, subject-tracked sequence at another aspect ratio (Premiere 14.0+).
use_for: Turning a 16:9 documentary cut into a 9:16 reel or 1:1 post
cards.how: var reel = seq.autoReframeSequence(9, 16, 'default', 'MyCut_9x16', false); motionPreset is 'slower', 'default' or 'faster'.
cards.script_api: Sequence.autoReframeSequence(numerator, denominator, motionPreset, newName, useNestedSequences) -> Sequence
cards.limits: Analysis is slow and can mis-frame (two-shots, text on screen): QC every shot and fix Position keys. On-screen graphics designed for 16:9 will be cropped. The 'Auto Reframe' effect (AE.ADBE AEFilterAutoFramer) is the per-clip version.

cards.name: Selection, linking and Scene Edit Detection
cards.summary: Selects timeline clips from a script, links/unlinks A/V, and runs Premiere's cut detection on the selection.
use_for: Splitting an imported finished video (news clip, archival reel) into shots before re-editing
Adding markers at every shot change for a montage plan
cards.how: trackItem.setSelected(1, 1); seq.performSceneEditDetectionOnSelection('ApplyCuts', true, 'MediumSensitivity'). actionDesired: 'ApplyCuts' or 'CreateMarkers'; sensitivity: 'LowSensitivity', 'MediumSensitivity', 'HighSensitivity'. Read selection with seq.getSelection().
cards.script_api: TrackItem.setSelected(state, updateUI); TrackItem.isSelected(); Sequence.getSelection(); Sequence.linkSelection(); Sequence.unlinkSelection(); Sequence.performSceneEditDetectionOnSelection(actionDesired, applyCutsToLinkedAudio, sensitivity); Sequence.isDoneAnalyzingForVideoEffects(); UXP: SequenceUtils.performSceneEditDetectionOnSelection(clipOperation, trackItemSelection)
cards.limits: The docs only say the call returns a boolean; whether all cuts exist when it returns is undocumented. Re-read the track after the call, and again after a pause, until the clip count stops changing. Not yet exercised in AdobeBridge.

cards.name: Track state: mute, lock, targeting
cards.summary: Mutes, locks and targets tracks; reads track names and clip/transition collections.
use_for: Muting a scratch VO track before export
Targeting tracks before insert edits or createSubsequence

cards.name: Clip speed and reverse (Speed/Duration)

cards.name: Time Remapping (speed ramps on the clip)

cards.script_api: none
cards.limits: Not in the ExtendScript docs or the UXP reference (checked through 26.5). Keyframed speed in imported FCP XML is converted to one constant average speed.

cards.name: Scriptable slow motion and speed ramps: Timewarp effect
cards.summary: Premiere 26 ships the AE Timewarp effect (match name AE.ADBE Timewarp). It retimes footage INSIDE the clip with a keyframable 'Speed' and optical-flow interpolation, and it can be applied and keyed from a script, so it is the practical scripted speed tool.
use_for: Smooth slow motion on a key moment in a documentary or trailer
Fast-slow-fast speed ramps on action beats in reels
Freeze-like holds by mapping 'Source Frame'
cards.how: QE: qeItem.addVideoEffect(qe.project.getVideoEffectByName('Timewarp')); then on the TrackItem's 'Timewarp' component set 'Speed' (harvest range -5000..5000, default 50), 'Method' (0..2, default 2), 'Adjust Time By' (0 = Speed, 1 = Source Frame), keyframe 'Speed' for ramps. PVE spec: {"name": "Timewarp", "pr_props": {"Speed": [[0, 100], [0.5, 30], [1.5, 30], [2, 100]]}}.
cards.script_api: QE: qeTrackItem.addVideoEffect(qe.project.getVideoEffectByName('Timewarp')); DOM: ComponentParam 'Speed', 'Method', 'Adjust Time By', 'Source Frame' setValue/addKey/setValueAtKey; UXP: VideoFilterFactory.createComponent('AE.ADBE Timewarp')
cards.limits: The clip's timeline length does NOT change: slowing shows only the first part of the source range; speeding past 100 runs out of frames and holds, so give the clip enough source. Pixel-motion warping on crowds, flags and hair. Heavier render. Applied and harvested without error on 26.0.2; the retime look itself is not yet verified in an AdobeBridge build.

cards.name: Lumetri Color from a script (incl. Look and LUT selection)

The Creative 'Intensity' is 'Intensity#2' (0..200, default 100); the first 'Intensity' (0..100, default 50) sits in Basic Correction before the Color group. cards.limits: The index-to-Look-name mapping was not harvested (render a gallery before choosing). cards.name: UXP Premiere API: overview and versions
cards.summary: Adobe's modern JavaScript (ES6+, async) plugin API for Premiere: `const ppro = require('premierepro')`. Public beta in 25.2 (Dec 2024), official in 25.6, the only surface getting new features (26.2 hybrid C++ plugins, 26.3 and 26.5 additions).

Undoable, grouped edits (transactions)
Transcripts, OTIO export (newer builds)

TypeScript types: github.com/adobe/premierepro-types. Each member lists the version it appeared in.
cards.script_api: require('premierepro'): Project, Sequence, SequenceEditor, VideoTrack/AudioTrack/CaptionTrack, VideoClipTrackItem/AudioClipTrackItem, VideoComponentChain/AudioComponentChain, VideoFilterFactory, AudioFilterFactory, TransitionFactory, ComponentParam, Keyframe, Markers, EncoderManager, Exporter, Transcript, ClipProjectItem, TickTime, Constants
cards.limits: Installed Premiere is 26.0.2: everything marked 25.6 is available, anything marked 26.2, 26.3 or 26.5 is NOT (e.g. ProjectConverter, createSubClipAction, WorkAreaUtils, createSequenceWithPresetPath). Some class pages say 'Since 25.6' for members the changelog lists as added in 26.5 (Transcript.transcribeClipProjectItem, isLanguagePackAvailable): trust the changelog and probe. Several calls were buggy before 26.5 (ClipProjectItem.createSetInPointAction/createSetOutPointAction errored, Markers.getMarkers(filters) threw, importAEComps without a bin could resolve true and add nothing). Most methods are async (await them); some are synchronous (lockedAccess, executeTransaction, SequenceEditor.getEditor, EncoderManager.getManager, setSelection since 26.3). Runs only inside a plugin: AdobeBridge's BridgeTalk/ExtendScript route cannot call it. No speed setter, no time remap, no nest, no adjustment-layer creation, no preset application in the reference (checked to 26.5).

cards.name: UXP: transactions and Actions (lockedAccess, executeTransaction)

cards.name: UXP plugin hosting and external control (UDT, Developer Mode, WebSocket, hybrid plugins)
cards.summary: UXP code runs only as a loaded plugin; there is no command-line or file-menu way to run a UXP script. External tools drive it by having the plugin open a WebSocket to a local server.
use_for: Planning a UXP route for AdobeBridge (for example to remove effects or add transitions by match name)
cards.how: Enable Premiere Settings > Plugins > 'Enable developer mode' and restart Premiere (Adobe's prerequisite for loading plugins with UXP Developer Tool 2.2+ on Premiere 25.6+; developer mode must also be on in UDT), load the plugin folder with UXP Developer Tool (UDT) or install a packaged .ccx. Pattern used by Premiere MCP bridges: the plugin's WebSocket client connects to a local Node/Python server, receives commands, runs them with require('premierepro') and replies. 26.2+ allows hybrid plugins with native C++ modules.

cards.limits: Plugin must be loaded in a running Premiere (UDT session or installed .ccx); a crash or restart unloads a UDT-loaded plugin. A UXP plugin cannot call ExtendScript, so an ExtendScript pipeline and a UXP plugin are two separate routes. Hybrid plugins need 26.2+.
